ai_analysis.problem: The fixed spinner is a modal overlay that blocks all page content and transitions during loading, causing a severe UX impact. This block prevents user interaction while the data is loading.
ai_analysis.original_code:
v-if="isLoading"
        class="fixed inset-0 bg-black bg-opacity-20 z-50 flex items-center justify-center"
ai_analysis.fixed_code:
v-if="isLoading"
        class="fixed inset-0 bg-black bg-opacity-20 z-50 flex items-center justify-center transition-opacity duration-300 ease-in-out"
ai_analysis.explanation: Adding the `transition-opacity duration-300 ease-in-out` CSS property will provide a smooth fade-in/fade-out effect for the loading overlay, reducing the visual impact and improving the user experience. This addresses both the UX and performance issues.
ai_analysis.fix_diff:
--- original
+++ fixed
@@ -14 +14 @@
- v-if="isLoading"
+ v-if="isLoading"
        class="fixed inset-0 bg-black bg-opacity-20 z-50 flex items-center justify-center"

ai_analysis.problem: The dynamic content within the `optionList` is not provided a unique key, causing React to unnecessarily re-render the component upon each iteration. This negatively impacts performance and can cause issues with screen readers.
ai_analysis.explanation: By utilizing the `option.type` as the unique key, this solution ensures that the component is only re-rendered when the `option` object itself changes, improving performance and accessibility.

ui_accessibility_analysis.problem: The `collapse-arrow` class doesn't provide ARIA attributes to enhance screen reader accessibility. The icon is visually dependent on the state, but screen readers aren't informed.
ui_accessibility_analysis.explanation: By adding `aria-expanded` the screen reader can be informed about the state of the component.
ui_accessibility_analysis.fix_diff:
--- original
+++ fixed
@@ -97 +97 @@
- :class="{ open: expandedOption === option.type }"
+ :class="{ open: expandedOption === option.type, 'aria-expanded': expandedOption === option.type }"

visual_simulation.layout_assessment: The layout remains consistent. The code has been refactored to improve performance and accessibility.
recommendations: Optimize loading spinner for a smoother UX.
Implement a unique key for dynamic elements to improve performance.

ui_accessibility_analysis.problem: The label text "Course Name:" is missing an accessibility role attribute, making it difficult for screen readers to interpret the content.  This violates accessibility guidelines for screen reader users.
ui_accessibility_analysis.original_code:
h1 class="text-center mb-2 subject-info">
        <div class="label">Course Name:</div
ui_accessibility_analysis.fixed_code:
h1 class="text-center mb-2 subject-info" role="presentation">
        <div class="label">Course Name:</div
ui_accessibility_analysis.explanation: Adding `role="presentation"` to the `h1` element provides a semantic label for the content, allowing screen readers to correctly identify and announce the course name. This is a standard accessibility practice.
ui_accessibility_analysis.fix_diff:
--- original
+++ fixed
@@ -38 +38 @@
- h1 class="text-center mb-2 subject-info">
+ h1 class="text-center mb-2 subject-info" role="presentation">

visual_simulation.layout_assessment: The addition of `role="presentation"` does not impact the layout. The content remains aligned and readable.
recommendations: Consider using a `<label>` element with the `for` attribute to explicitly associate the label with the input field, further enhancing accessibility.
Ensure sufficient color contrast between the label and the course name text for users with visual impairments.
